message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season, which typically occurs from late winter to early spring. Male lions form coalitions and compete for dominance; the alpha male will guard females and defend their territory. When a female is in estrus (lasting only a few days), she signals her readiness through scent marking and vocalizations. Males may engage in displays such as roaring, scent-marking, and physical contests to win access. Once a male wins, he mounts the female and copulation lasts only a few minutes. After mating, the male may stay nearby to protect the female and her offspring.
